question: A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

options.opd: The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and laboratory findings suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), including arthritis, pleuritis, malar rash, and positive antinuclear and anti-DNA antibodies. The initial treatment for mild to moderate SLE, particularly with joint and skin involvement, typically includes non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and antimalarials like hydroxychloroquine. High-dose glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants like mycophenolate are generally reserved for more severe organ involvement or refractory cases.
